sn48.18:1.6: While it the five qualities of faith, etc., are found among those who are unenlightened, and even, as potential, among all beings, it is only on entering the noble path that they are considered “faculties” with the decisive power to overcome their opposites. | The expression “stands outside in the faction of ordinary persons” is found only here and SN 55.40:2.1. In both cases it indicates individuals who are not noble ones, but who nonetheless may be Buddhists. Bāhira (“outside”) here should be distinguished from the more common bāhiraka (“outsider”), which refers to non-Buddhists.
